page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance belonging to the Famsv6 server family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core execution, database operations, and cryptography tasks perform within the average range. However, a notable hardware tradeoff exists in memory subsystem performance: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance provides a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is suitable for database operations, text processing, software compilation, and small-to-medium language model inference. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs positions this server as a cost-efficient option for memory-heavy workloads relying on network-attached premium storage.
